$comment: Machine-readable crosswalk between the G7 AI bill of materials minimum elements and the two SBOM formats. Data only. No conformance policy is expressed here.

specification.title: Software Bill of Materials for AI - Minimum Elements
specification.dateNote: The document itself carries no date beyond the year 2026 and no version number. 2026-05-12 is the publication date on the BSI landing page; CISA announced it on 2026-05-13. The 2026-06-16 date seen in some write-ups is a law firm client alert, not the guidance.
specification.accessNote: cisa.gov returns HTTP 403 to automated requests. BSI is a co-publisher and hosts the identical original.
specification.mandatoryQuote: These minimum elements are not mandatory; do not create requirements, standards, or legislation.

sitsOnTopOf.title: 2026 Minimum Elements for a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)
sitsOnTopOf.quote: The minimum elements in an SBOM for AI are in addition to the general SBOM minimum elements.

cyclonedx-1.7.name: CycloneDX
cyclonedx-1.7.note: The AI object graph is structurally identical between 1.6 and 1.7. modelCard arrived in 1.5, environmentalConsiderations in 1.6.

spdx-3.0.1.name: SPDX
spdx-3.0.1.standard: ISO/IEC 5962:2021 covers version 2.2.1 only; 3.x is not yet published as an ISO standard
spdx-3.0.1.note: Version 3.1 is a release candidate only as of 2026-08-29.

fitScale.direct: The format has a purpose-built field that carries this element.
fitScale.partial: A field exists but is narrower, differently scoped, or uses an incompatible vocabulary.
fitScale.properties-only: Expressible only through a free-form property bag or an external link. Not interoperable.

conformanceNote: The source specification assigns no required, optional or recommended level to any element, and uses no RFC 2119 keywords. Every element here is marked 'unspecified'. Any conformance policy is the implementer's own and should be declared as such.

clusters.name: Metadata
clusters.scope: Information about the AI bill of materials itself, not about the components it describes.

elements.name: SBOM author
elements.captures: Entity that generated the SBOM. Distinct from the producer of the thing described.
elements.statedConstraint: String. Full names, no acronyms unless official.

elements.name: SBOM version
elements.captures: Version of the SBOM document itself, per component name/version pair.
elements.statedConstraint: SemVer 2.0.0 (major SHOULD be 1) or RFC 9562 UUID.
elements.note: CDX version is an integer, not SemVer. SPDX 3.0.1 has no SBOM document version at all. Real gap in both.

elements.name: SBOM data format name
elements.captures: Which format this SBOM is written in.

elements.name: SBOM data format version
elements.captures: Version of that format. Deprecated versions should not be used.

elements.name: SBOM author signature
elements.captures: Digital signature of the SBOM author, for integrity and authenticity.
elements.statedConstraint: Algorithm approved by NIST DSS, ISO/IEC 14888-4:2024 or ENISA. No format named.
elements.note: THE COMMERCIAL HOOK. CycloneDX has a signature slot; SPDX 3.0.1 does not, so SPDX signing is out of band. Neither spec names a signature format (no Sigstore, DSSE, JWS or in-toto).

elements.name: SBOM tool name
elements.captures: Tool the author used to build the SBOM.

elements.name: SBOM tool version
elements.captures: Version of that tool. If none, say 'unknown'.
elements.note: Empty is non-conformant. Explicit 'unknown' is conformant. Neither format enforces this.

elements.name: SBOM generation context
elements.captures: Lifecycle phase at which the SBOM was made.
elements.statedConstraint: Open list. Examples: before build, build, after build.

paths: metadata.lifecycles[].phase (design, pre-build, build, post-build, operations, discovery, decommission)
LifecycleScopeType on relationships (design, build, development, test, runtime, other)

elements.note: Vocabularies do not line up with each other or with the spec's three example values. SPDX scopes relationships, not the document.

elements.name: SBOM timestamp
elements.captures: When the SBOM data was last changed. Every version gets a new one.
elements.note: RFC 9557 permits suffixes such as [America/Chicago] that RFC 3339 validators reject. Both formats validate as plain date-time, so a strictly conformant timestamp can fail their schemas.

elements.name: SBOM dependency relationship
elements.captures: Component X includes Y; or Y is derived from or a descendant of Z.
elements.statedConstraint: Values: includes, included in, plus derived-from and descendant-of semantics.

paths: Relationship: contains, dependsOn, ancestorOf, descendantOf, hasVariant

clusters.name: System Level Properties
clusters.scope: The AI system as a whole, including systems composed of several AI elements such as classifiers, large language models or agents. Covers software dependencies and frameworks, and how components interact and process user data.

elements.name: System name
elements.captures: Human-readable name of the whole AI system.
elements.statedConstraint: Multi-valued: alternate names should be capturable.
elements.note: Neither format allows alternate names on a single component. Spec explicitly asks for multiple entries. Use properties or externalIdentifier as a workaround.

elements.name: System components
elements.captures: Everything included in the AI system: models, databases, tools.

elements.name: System producer
elements.captures: Entity that creates, defines and identifies the system.

elements.name: System version
elements.captures: Version of the system. If none, say 'unknown'.

elements.name: System timestamp
elements.captures: Last update to the system, including model or software updates.
elements.statedConstraint: No RFC constraint stated (unlike SBOM timestamp).
elements.note: SPDX is materially better here. CycloneDX has no component-level 'last updated' field.

elements.name: System data flow
elements.captures: Data movement between components: endpoints, APIs, agent protocols, external services.

paths: services[].data[] with flow (inbound, outbound, bi-directional, unknown) and classification

elements.note: CycloneDX SaaSBOM services model this properly. SPDX 3.0.1 cannot express data flow at all. Biggest single divergence between the two formats.

elements.name: System data usage
elements.captures: How data is processed and consumed, including logging and derived metadata.
elements.note: Both weak. No structured notion of 'is user input used for training'.

elements.name: System input/output properties
elements.captures: Input and output types, modality, preprocessing, tokenizer.
elements.note: CycloneDX allows exactly ONE key here (format) because inputOutputMLParameters is additionalProperties:false. Modality lives in the separate cdx:ai-ml property taxonomy, not the schema. This is model-level in CDX, not system-level.

elements.name: Intended application area
elements.captures: Domain the system is deployed in: healthcare, finance, cybersecurity, real time.
elements.note: SPDX has a purpose-built field. CycloneDX only has model-level use cases.

clusters.name: Models
clusters.scope: Identifies the models used by the system, describes how each model's weights were produced, and outlines their properties and limitations.

elements.name: Model name
elements.captures: Human-readable model name.
elements.statedConstraint: Multi-valued: alternate names should be capturable.
elements.note: Same alternate-names gap as System name.

elements.name: Model identifier
elements.captures: One or more machine-readable identifiers.
elements.statedConstraint: CPE, PURL, UUID, org IDs, commit hashes, OmniBOR, SWHID. Include ALL of them.
elements.note: Both support the named schemes. Hugging Face PURL type (pkg:huggingface/...) is the de facto model identifier.

elements.name: Model version
elements.captures: Model version. If none, say 'unknown'.

elements.name: Model timestamp
elements.captures: Last update to the model, or its production release date.
elements.note: SPDX better.

elements.name: Model producer
elements.captures: Who pre-trained, post-trained or fine-tuned the model. Also the security point of contact.

elements.name: Model description
elements.captures: Capabilities, known limitations, and lineage including the predecessor model.
elements.note: LINEAGE IS THE PROBLEM. CycloneDX pedigree is structured but generic. SPDX 3.0.1 has no base-model edge at all, and even 3.1-dev's finetunedOn points at a dataset, not a parent model. 'This was fine-tuned from Llama 3' has no interoperable representation in either format.

elements.name: Model hash value
elements.captures: Hash of the weights or model file.

elements.name: Model hash algorithm
elements.captures: Algorithm that produced the hash.
elements.statedConstraint: IANA Hash Function Textual Names. NIST-approved.

paths: components[].hashes[].alg (closed enum: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256/384/512, SHA3-*, BLAKE2b-*, BLAKE3)

elements.note: NEITHER FORMAT USES IANA NAMES. Both have their own closed enums. A conformance checker has to map IANA names onto each format's vocabulary, and the sets do not fully overlap.

elements.name: Model properties
elements.captures: Architecture, parameter count, network type, hyperparameters. Explicitly nestable.

paths: modelCard.modelParameters.approach.type (enum: supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement-learning, semi-supervised, self-supervised), .task, .architectureFamily, .modelArchitecture

elements.note: CycloneDX is richer via the property taxonomy but the taxonomy sits outside the schema. SPDX hyperparameters are untyped strings with no units.

elements.name: Model input-output properties
elements.captures: Input and output types, context length, modality, tokenizer.
elements.note: Context length and modality have no schema home in either format. CycloneDX puts modality in the taxonomy (cdx:ai-ml:model:modality); context length only as a hyperparameter property.

elements.name: Model training properties
elements.captures: All training: pre-training, fine-tuning, continual learning, RLHF, DPO, PPO, GRPO.

paths: cdx:ai-ml:model:parameter:tune_method (full, sft, rlhf, adapter, prompt, lora, alora, qlora)

elements.note: CycloneDX formulation can model the actual training run as a workflow. SPDX models it as a Build. Both are possible, neither is conventional, and no two producers will do it the same way.

elements.name: Model license
elements.captures: Licence type, and whether open weight, open architecture, open data or open training.
elements.statedConstraint: Link to licence doc, or the SPDX/CDX licence fields.

paths: hasDeclaredLicense and hasConcludedLicense relationships (exactly one of each REQUIRED on an AIPackage)

elements.note: OPEN-WEIGHT VOCABULARY IS MISSING EVERYWHERE. Neither format has any way to say open weight vs open architecture vs open data vs open training. This is a named requirement with no representation.

elements.name: Model external references
elements.captures: Links to model cards, system cards, papers, documentation.

paths: components[].externalReferences[] (47-value type enum incl. model-card, documentation, attestation, threat-model, adversary-model, risk-assessment, certification-report, pentest-report)

elements.note: CycloneDX has a dedicated model-card reference type. SPDX external refs are less typed.

clusters.name: Datasets Properties
clusters.scope: Datasets used during the whole lifecycle of the model, including the information that documents identity and provenance.

elements.name: Dataset name
elements.captures: Name given by the dataset creator.

elements.name: Dataset description
elements.captures: What the dataset is for: pre-training, fine-tuning, benchmark, evaluation. Public or private.

elements.name: Dataset content
elements.captures: What is in it and in what shape: financial, medical, image, audio, JSON, XML.

paths: componentData.type (enum: source-code, configuration, dataset, definition, other)
DatasetPackage.datasetType (14-value enum: audio, categorical, graph, image, noAssertion, numeric, other, sensor, structured, syntactic, text, timeseries, timestamp, video)

elements.note: SPDX is clearly better. Its 14-value datasetType is the only real content vocabulary in either format, and it is the ONLY required property in the whole SPDX AI/Dataset surface (minCount 1).

elements.name: Dataset identifier
elements.captures: Unique identification of the dataset.

elements.name: Dataset hash
elements.captures: Hash over the dataset file.
elements.statedConstraint: No algorithm field is defined (unlike Models).

paths: components[].hashes[] on the wrapping component only

elements.note: TRAP: CycloneDX componentData has NO hash property of its own. You can only hash the wrapping component. Also note the spec itself omits a Dataset hash algorithm element, which is an asymmetry with the Models cluster.

elements.name: Dataset provenance
elements.captures: Origin, collection method (web crawl, commercial agreement), post-processing, curation, labelling, creator, synthetic-data method.
elements.note: SPDX has purpose-built fields for collection and preprocessing. CycloneDX has stewardship roles SPDX lacks. Neither has a synthetic-data-method field.

elements.name: Dataset statistical properties
elements.captures: Mean, variance, median, mode, range, skewness across the dataset lifecycle.
elements.note: REAL GAP IN BOTH. No statistical characterisation exists anywhere in either format. Nearest is SPDX datasetNoise (free text) and CycloneDX graphics (base64 images).

elements.name: Dataset sensitivity
elements.captures: Whether it contains PII, freely accessible, copyright-protected, sensitive (financial, medical) or national-security data.
elements.note: SPDX has controlled vocabularies, CycloneDX has none. But NEITHER covers copyright-protected or national-security categories, which the spec names explicitly. SPDX 3.1-dev adds amberStrict.

elements.name: Dataset dependency relationship
elements.captures: Software used to create, modify and maintain the dataset. Derivation from another dataset.
elements.note: Both express it, neither conventionally.

elements.name: Dataset license
elements.captures: Licence type of the dataset.

paths: hasDeclaredLicense and hasConcludedLicense (exactly one each REQUIRED on a DatasetPackage)

clusters.name: Infrastructure
clusters.scope: Physical and virtual infrastructure critical to running and supporting the AI system, including a link to a hardware bill of materials where one exists.

elements.name: Infrastructure software
elements.captures: Firmware, package managers, third-party libraries, frameworks, runtimes, tools needed to run the system.

elements.name: Infrastructure hardware
elements.captures: Link to an existing HBOM covering the hardware the system runs on.
elements.note: SPDX 3.0.1 cannot express hardware at all. CycloneDX can link a separate BOM but has no HBOM profile either. Note OMB M-26-05 now makes agencies inventory hardware as well as software, so this gap has a buyer.

clusters.name: Security Properties
clusters.scope: Cybersecurity measures that apply to the AI models and systems.

elements.name: Security controls
elements.captures: General controls (encryption, data minimisation, differential privacy, access control, API auth, anomaly detection) AND AI-specific controls (adversarial robustness training, prompt injection controls, I/O filters, training-data curation).
elements.statedConstraint: Free, may link to a framework.
elements.note: THE BIGGEST GAP ON THIS SHEET. Neither format has ANY field for adversarial robustness, prompt injection resistance, jailbreak resistance, data poisoning, watermarking, guardrails or red-teaming. Zero hits for all of those terms in both schemas. This is unclaimed territory.

elements.name: Security compliance
elements.captures: Certification schemes, standards or frameworks the model or system complies with.
elements.note: SPDX has a plain field. CycloneDX requires the heavier Attestations construct.

elements.name: Cybersecurity policy information
elements.captures: Link to the producer's published security.txt.
elements.note: Neither has a security.txt reference type by name. Nearest fit only.

elements.name: Vulnerability referencing
elements.captures: Link to databases or repositories showing exploitability of known vulnerabilities.

paths: vulnerabilities[] (CVE, CWE, CVSS ratings, VEX analysis state)
Security profile: Vulnerability, VulnAssessmentRelationship, VEX relationships, CVSS v2/v3/v4, EPSS, SSVC

elements.note: Both strong, but both are CVE-shaped. Neither can express a model-level attack surface, only vulnerabilities in software dependencies.

clusters.name: Key Performance Indicators
clusters.scope: Indicators for the AI system and its components, focusing on their lifecycle phases.

elements.name: Security metrics
elements.captures: Metrics for the security characteristics of the models or the system, such as robustness benchmarks.

paths: modelCard.quantitativeAnalysis.performanceMetrics[] (type free text, value is a STRING, optional slice and confidence interval)

elements.note: Untyped in both. No units, no thresholds beyond SPDX metricDecisionThreshold, no security semantics. And in CycloneDX there is NO field linking a metric to the dataset it was measured on.

elements.name: Operational performance KPIs
elements.captures: Uptime, incident resolution time, latency, request throughput, load balancing.
elements.note: REAL GAP IN BOTH. No operational-telemetry concept exists in either format. This is arguably out of scope for a static BOM, and worth saying so.
